discoveries.headline: What bitcoin ETF outflows are telling us
discoveries.why: US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $306.4 million in a single day last week, taking their combined assets down to $77.7 billion and 2026 net outflows past $2.5 billion. Cointelegraph's Helen Partz shows where the coins sit (about 1.25 million BTC across the funds) and notes long-term holders have been trimming too. A clear way to see how big money is moving in and out of crypto. Education, not advice.

discoveries.headline: No treaty yet on killer robots
discoveries.why: After a week of talks in Geneva, the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons closed on 21 November with what campaigners call a watered-down mandate that sets no clear path to a binding treaty on autonomous weapons. More than 95 states backed a treaty during the week, and the press release quotes Stop Killer Robots, Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International on what happens next. It's the campaigners' view, and a clear account of a decision that will shape how wars are fought.
discoveries.meta_credit: Stop Killer Robots · press release, Geneva

discoveries.headline: A tardigrade lays her eggs in her old skin
discoveries.why: Biologist Gonzalo Quiroga-Artigas caught a tiny tardigrade under the microscope as she shed her skin and left her eggs inside it, a portrait that placed 12th in the 2026 Nikon Small World competition. ZME Science explains this odd nursery, and reminds us these are the animals that survived open space on a 10-day European Space Agency mission in 2007. Small wonders, up close.
discoveries.credit: Photo: Dr Gonzalo Quiroga Artigas / Nikon Small World

discoveries.headline: The Dalai Lama on facing life's problems
discoveries.why: In just over a minute, the Dalai Lama shares realistic advice from the Indian master Shantideva on meeting life's problems with a calm, confident mind, free from needless worry. Worry adds weight before anything has even happened, so this is a short way to set it down before the day takes off. Recorded in Leh, Ladakh, in 2018 and shared by his office this month.
discoveries.source: The Office of His Holiness the Dalai Lama
discoveries.meta_credit: dalailama.com · recorded in Leh, Ladakh, 2 Aug 2018

discoveries.headline: The surgeon who inspired Sherlock Holmes
discoveries.why: Historian of medicine Lindsey Fitzharris tells Sean Carroll about two pioneers: Joseph Bell, the Scottish surgeon and forensic pathologist who inspired Sherlock Holmes, and Harold Gillies, who pioneered reconstructive surgery. Bell is the subject of her new book Sleuth-Hound, Gillies of The Facemaker. A gripping 72 minutes for the commute on how careful observation changed medicine.
discoveries.meta_credit: Mindscape · Sean Carroll with Lindsey Fitzharris

discoveries.headline: Steve Kilbey's Lacuna, and a tour with an orchestra
discoveries.why: The Church's Steve Kilbey is Australian Musician's Musician of the Month, talking with Greg Phillips about Lacuna, a 17-track double album recorded in Austin, Texas, with producer Daryl Thorp. He's touring it now as A Psychedelic Symphony with a 30-piece orchestra under George Ellis, through to Adelaide on 28 November. A long, warm conversation with one of our most lasting songwriters.

discoveries.headline: Can yoga slow ageing? What the evidence says
discoveries.why: A new review in Cureus by researchers in Jamshedpur, India, finds yoga reliably improves flexibility, balance and leg strength in older adults, but did not show that it reverses ageing or extends lifespan. News-Medical walks through the findings, from modest drops in blood pressure to early lab markers that still need proper trials. An honest look at what a daily practice can and can't do. General information, not medical advice.

discoveries.headline: Ten minutes of morning yoga with Rolf Gates
discoveries.why: Yoga teacher Rolf Gates leads a gentle ten-minute series to wake you up, starting in mountain pose with arm sweeps and slow breathing through the nose. He keeps the focus on the breath, so it suits any body and any level. An easy morning ritual before the day gets busy.
discoveries.published_date: Evergreen video (AARP; date not shown on the page)

discoveries.headline: Build strength with just a mat
discoveries.why: Strength coach Esme Hovekamp designed this no-equipment workout for beginners: nine holds, from glute bridges and bird dogs to side planks and a hollow body hold, each held for 10 to 30 seconds. It takes 25 to 35 minutes, and you can do it up to three or four times a week. A simple way to start if the gym feels like a lot.
discoveries.meta_credit: The Irish Times · Anna Maltby (originally in The New York Times)
